title: The Queen
subtitle: Rook plus bishop in one — your strongest piece.
goals: Move the queen along ranks, files and diagonals
Capture safely — the queen is too valuable to lose

steps.say: Meet the queen — a rook and a bishop rolled into one. Straight lines AND diagonals, any distance. From the center she controls 27 squares!
Watch her work — rook move, then bishop move.

autoMoves.say: ...and back across like lightning. Powerful — but remember: lose the queen and you usually lose the game.

steps.prompt: Move your queen to the h8 corner — one move, whole board.
hints: h8 shares a diagonal with d4.
Slide up the dark diagonal: d4, e5, f6, g7... all the way home.
steps.wrongSay: Not h8. The corner is one diagonal slide away from d4.
steps.successSay: Across the whole board in one move — and she even announces check from there. That's queen power.

steps.prompt: Capture all three black pawns with your queen.
hints: The queen combines rook lines and bishop diagonals — every pawn is reachable if you pick the right order.
Start with the pawn on your diagonal, then use ranks and files.

sequenceGoal.say: Munch! Now find the line to the next one.

steps.wrongSay: No pawn on that square. Check every rank, file and diagonal from where your queen stands.
steps.successSay: Three pawns, three moves. Nothing hides from a centralized queen.

steps.prompt: One pawn is free, one is poisoned. Capture the safe one!
hints: A queen for a pawn is the worst trade in chess. Check who defends each pawn.
The d5 pawn is guarded by the pawn on c6. The g4 pawn stands alone.

line.say: Correct! The g4 pawn had no bodyguard — a clean snack for the queen.

rejections.say: cxd5! You just traded the most powerful piece on the board for a single pawn. Always check a pawn's bodyguards.

steps.wrongSay: One of those pawns can be taken for free. Count defenders before the queen commits.
steps.successSay: That care is exactly how you keep a queen alive all game.

hints: The black king is boxed in by his own pawns. Which rank is fatally weak?
Send the queen to the back rank — no defender can stop her.

line.say: Checkmate! The back rank was undefended, and the king's own pawns became his prison.

rejections.say: A fine central square — but no mate. The kill shot is on the back rank, where the king can't escape his pawn wall.

steps.wrongSay: Not mate. Look at the king's row — can he ever leave it?
steps.successSay: The back-rank mate with a queen — you'll see this pattern in real games constantly.
